title: Nothing can resolve internal service names
intro: Multiple teams are reporting their services can't reach each other by name — 'could not resolve host' errors everywhere, all at once, across unrelated apps.

steps.prompt: Multiple unrelated services failing at the same time points at shared infrastructure, not one app. Check the CoreDNS pods first.
steps.fake_output:
NAME                       READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
coredns-5d78c9869d-2xk9p   0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   6          8m
coredns-5d78c9869d-9jz3q   0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   6          8m
steps.hint: DNS in Kubernetes is itself just a Deployment (CoreDNS) running in kube-system — check it like any other workload.

steps.prompt: Both CoreDNS replicas are crash-looping. Check why.
steps.fake_output: plugin/loop: Loop (127.0.0.1:52931 -> :53) detected for zone ".", see https://coredns.io/plugins/loop#troubleshooting. Query: "HINFO"
steps.hint: CoreDNS logs its own reason for exiting on crash — no need to guess.

steps.prompt: That's a DNS forwarding loop — CoreDNS is somehow forwarding queries back to itself. Check its ConfigMap for the upstream forwarding config.
expected_commands: kubectl get configmap coredns -n kube-system -o yaml
steps.hint: The Corefile's 'forward' directive controls where unresolved queries go — that's the likely culprit.

steps.prompt: The node's /etc/resolv.conf was recently changed to point at this cluster's own DNS, creating the loop CoreDNS detected. After fixing the Corefile to forward to a real external resolver, confirm CoreDNS recovers.
steps.fake_output:
NAME                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
coredns-5d78c9869d-2xk9p   1/1     Running   6          9m
coredns-5d78c9869d-9jz3q   1/1     Running   6          9m
steps.hint: After editing the ConfigMap, CoreDNS pods need to pick up the change — a rollout restart applies it.

resolution: A node-level change to /etc/resolv.conf pointed the host's own DNS resolution at the cluster's CoreDNS service, and CoreDNS's Corefile was configured to forward unresolved queries to /etc/resolv.conf — creating an infinite loop that CoreDNS's built-in loop detection correctly caught and refused to run with, crash-looping instead of serving broken DNS silently. Every service in the cluster depends on CoreDNS for internal name resolution, which is why the outage looked unrelated across completely different apps — the actual failure was in shared infrastructure, not any of the apps reporting the symptom.
